title: Flash + PagedKV + Continuous Batching: regression audit and prompt-set diffs
content:
Summary:

This note records the regression audit we ran after rolling three runtime kernel changes into the nightly branch: 1) upstream flash-attention rewrite (vectorized kernels + alternative tiling), 2) paged KV-store prototype (heap-backed KV with eviction), and 3) continuous batching scheduler adjustments (aggressive batching windows for low qps). The purpose: identify functional and quality regressions on onboarding evals and prompt sets used by Applied ML when certifying open-model variants for production.

Context and motivation:
- Flash-attention: expected throughput win (~+15–40% tokens/s) for long sequences; potential numerical differences in attention accumulation and fp16 reduction order.
- PagedKV: reduces GPU memory for very long-context sessions by paging inactive KV to host memory; possible changes in exact generation (timing of cache hits) and increased micro-latency for cache misses.
- Continuous batching: reduces per-token overhead by coalescing; risk is additional prompt mixing and slightly changed timing that interacts with KV caching and tokenization boundaries.

What we ran (high level):
- Baseline: nightly before the three patches (sha: a7f2db).
- Candidate: nightly + patches (sha: b3c9ff).
- Models: two representative open variants used by onboarding: redwood/open-v1-7b (quantized fp16) and community/llama-like-13b (int8 + HF compat).
- Eval suites: onboarding-classic (N=2.2k prompts across instruction-following, QA, summarization, code), convo-long-context (N=800, deliberately >4k token exchanges), and stability-checklist (N=300 targeted robustness prompts).
- Metrics captured: accuracy/EM where applicable, ROUGE-L for summarization, code-exec pass@1 (sanity), average log-prob delta on ground-truth tokens, embedding cosine similarity vs baseline outputs, and a small human spot-check for hallucination severity. Also capture latency and tokens/sec.

Key numeric diffs (candidate minus baseline):
- redwood/open-v1-7b:
  - onboarding-classic: accuracy -0.9% (from 84.7% -> 83.8%), ROUGE-L -0.7, avg_logprob -0.018, embed_cosine -0.002
  - convo-long-context: hallucination score (auto) +6% (worse), avg_logprob -0.035, tokens/s +22% (good)
  - stability-checklist: targeted factual inversion cases +3 failures (8 -> 11), code-exec pass@1 unchanged
- community/llama-like-13b:
  - onboarding-classic: accuracy -1.8%, ROUGE-L -1.1, avg_logprob -0.045, embed_cosine -0.007
  - convo-long-context: longer-context degradation larger: hallucination +11%, avg_logprob -0.072, tokens/s +18%

Observations and hypotheses:
1) Numerical order effects from flash-attention fp16 reductions cause small but consistent negative deltas on average log-prob and embedding similarity. These deltas are small but correlate with downstream metrics (ROUGE/accuracy) in proportion to sequence length. Hypothesis: reduction order and block tiling cause subtle softmax scaling changes on borderline tokens.
2) PagedKV changes: increased inconsistencies in convo-long-context outputs. We see a pattern where mid-conversation context (older KV pages) exhibit staleness: model sometimes repeats or incorrectly references earlier turns. Hypothesis: eviction timing and page rehydration latency lead to occasional KV misses at token generation boundaries, causing model to rely on a truncated context window.
3) Continuous batching: while throughput improved, micro-ordering of tokens from different requests occasionally interleaves states at the scheduler level in edge cases, particularly when combined with paged KV rehydration. This interaction surface is likely the driver for the larger regressions in long-context conversational evals.

Evidence from traces (spot examples):
- Example ID C-179: baseline correctly answers with entity "Maya Santoro" when referencing turn 2; candidate returned "Maya Santiago" (wrong surname). Token-level trace shows softmax score shift at token index 12 of the answer; attention maps differ in scale for a block where flash-attention uses a different reduction order.
- Example ID L-042 (convo-long): candidate response repeats an earlier user utterance; trace shows KV page fault at approx token 512 and rehydration gap of ~13ms, candidate resumed generation missing a token that established referent.

Risk assessment and severity:
- Severity: moderate (quality regressions are measurable, not catastrophic).
- Customer impact: increased hallucinations in long, multi-turn chat scenarios; small drop in instruction-following accuracy may affect downstream feature gating for model onboarding.
- Performance tradeoff: throughput and memory savings are significant (tokens/s +18–22%; per-session GPU memory down ~20% on long-context sessions), so rollback is not unequivocal.

Action items (short-term):
1) Revert the flash-attention tiling changes in the nightly and land a patch that preserves numeric reduction order (PR referenced). Temporarily pin kernels to existing reduction order in our model builds. Owner: Marcelo. ETA: 1 week.
2) Instrument paged KV: add metrics for eviction timestamps, page fault latencies, and token-indexed KV-hit traces in the serving logs. Owner: Dana. ETA: 3 days.
3) Add a scheduler-level isolation guard in continuous batching: if an in-flight request triggers KV rehydration, avoid coalescing its next token with unrelated requests for a short grace window. Owner: Tom. ETA: 10 days.
4) Expand the onboarding eval to include 1k additional long-context prompts (edge cases) and rerun diff after above changes. Owner: Aisha. ETA: 2 weeks.
5) Human review: triage top 50 regression examples, document whether regression is acceptable tradeoff given perf gains. Owner: Jaya. ETA: 1 week.

Open questions / discussion items:
- Acceptable numeric delta thresholds: current onboarding gating uses +/-1% accuracy for major releases. Should throughput/memory improvements allow a larger tolerance for minor quality drifts for minor model variants?
- Paging policy: would soft pinning of recent pages (LRU with small sticky window) reduce KV misses sufficiently without significant memory overhead?
- Could we add a micro-precision test harness (fp32 vs fp16) to flag when kernel reorderings change rank order of top-k token logits?

Notes to self / breadcrumbs for follow-up (informal):
- See github PR 1814 for the flash refactor; talk to kernel author (cc @marcelo) re: reduction commutativity tests.
- Attach CI trace dumps under artifacts/ci/2026-02-18/* (binary traces).
- Slack thread: #serving-runtime: flash-paged-regression (links in PR).
- Preliminary human spot-check: of 50 regression examples, 34 are subtle (name variants, tense flips), 16 are clear hallucinations or missed referents.

Conclusion (short):
We have a measurable tradeoff: good throughput and memory improvements vs modest quality regressions concentrated in long-context conversational workloads. Next steps are targeted kernel fixes (preserve reduction semantics), better KV paging heuristics, and batching isolation to avoid cross-request state coupling. After implementing the action items, rerun the onboarding evals and reconvene for a decision on whether to accept the runtime changes for onboarding model certification.

Appendix (quick checklist):
- [ ] Add per-token logprob diff exporter (action Dana)
- [ ] Deploy patched flash kernel to nightly-extra and run A/B 72-hr sweep (Marcelo)
- [ ] Add 1k long-context prompts (Aisha)
- [ ] Create JIRA epic to track follow-ups (JIRA-INF-4821)

End of note.
